abstract.t: PQST (Post-Quantum Secure Transport) is a post-quantum native session-primary datagram transport for secure tunnels without classical public key cryptography, hybrid key exchange, or classical fallback. Its central rule is that the cryptographic session is the persistent object and the network path is a replaceable carrier. A PQST session can outlive the complete loss of every network path and be re-anchored on a new path with fresh post-quantum key material, without the tunnel, its addressing, its authorization, or the peers' authenticated identities changing. PQST runs directly over UDP as one protocol with one state machine. Identities are ML-KEM-1024 keys and authentication is by decapsulation, so no signature is computed online. The same exchange that establishes a session also recovers it, re-proves it, and ratchets it. The per-packet overhead is 44 octets with the epoch and sequence number hidden, identifiers are derived rather than signalled, and every input that has not been authenticated costs a bounded amount and changes no authoritative state. PQST is designed as the substrate for group continuity across intermittent networks; its events are typed so that a layer above it can distinguish a transport event from a security event.
